newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: China's premier in Caracas on last leg of Latin tour.
newsitem.headline: China's premier in Caracas on last leg of Latin tour.

text.p: Chinese Prime Minister Li Peng arrived in Venezuela on Tuesday on the last leg of a South American tour aimed at strengthening China's still modest economic ties with the region.
Li, who earlier visited Chile and Brazil, is expected to sign deals on the supply of local trademark Orimulsion boiler fuel with state-run Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) oil giant.
The Chinese premier will also use his two-day visit to spell out China's economic strategy towards Latin America.
Li was met at Maiquetia international airport by acting President Jose Guillermo Andueza -- in the absence of President Rafael Caldera who had not yet returned from an Ibero-American summit in Chile.
The Chinese leader is due to address the Latin American Economic System (SELA), a Caracas-based regional economic think-tank, on Thursday.

Trade between China and Latin America and the Caribbean nearly tripled in five years to reach $6 billion in 1995, SELA figures show. More than a third of these commercial exchanges were with Brazil, Latin America's largest country.
Bilateral trade with Venezuela totalled a scant $1.68 million last year, sharply down from $20.09 million in 1994 when Venezuela exported a record $13 million of iron ore.
However, Venezuelan government officials expect these modest figures to greatly improve after Li's visit, the first ever by a Chinese premier to Venezuela.
The Venezuelan Foreign Ministry said Li would sign a memorandum of understanding for a feasibility study on a joint venture to build a $320-million Orimulsion plant in Venezuela.
Sometimes called by its critics "the world's filthiest fuel", Orimulsion is produced from an extra heavy bitumen-type oil found in large quantities in northern Venezuela.
PDVSA's affiliate Bitor has already supplied contracts for the heavy fuel with power generators in several countries, including the United States, Britain, Japan, Italy and Canada.
The plant, whose study should be completed next year, would produce 5.2 million tonnes per year, or about a quarter of Venezuela's planned Orimulsion output by the end of the decade.
Li, who is due to meet Caldera on Wednesday, is also expected to sign a long-term Orimulsion supply contract and a general agreement to cooperate in the hydrocarbons sector.
An accord will also be signed allowing Venezuela to maintain its consulate in Hong Kong when the British colony ia handed back to Beijing next July.
Officials said human rights issues were likely to be skirted in Caracas, as they were during the Chilean and Brazilian stops.
Chinese diplomats pointed to Li's answer on this in Santiago last week when he said China did not accept foreign interference in domestic issues.
Li ended his visit to Brazil with a two-day visit to the Amazon, where he traveled to the meeting place of Negro, Amazon and Solimoes rivers.
An Amazonas state spokesman said he lunched on local fresh-water fish and visited Chinese logging and industrial firms operating in the Manaus free-trade zone.
